title: Thermal Application
objective: Explain at knowledge level the effects of heating and cooling on metals, the purpose of controlled thermal treatment, and why thermal work requires authorised procedures, competent supervision and workplace safety controls.

verified_topic_elements: KT0101 — Theory of contraction and expansion — 30%
KT0102 — Types of hazards such as fire, equipment, ventilation, storage and consumables — 30%
KT0103 — Heat treatment methods and applications — 40%
curriculum_traceability.primary_source: QCTO occupational curriculum hosted by CHIETA — Curriculum-6.pdf

safety_boundary: Knowledge learning and safety awareness only. This lesson does not provide instructions for operating heating, welding or cutting equipment, handling fuel gases, performing heat treatment, setting temperatures, selecting process parameters, or carrying out practical thermal work. Practical activities belong in authorised occupational training and workplace processes under competent supervision.

sections.heading: 1. What thermal application means
sections.body: Thermal application concerns how heat and cooling affect metal during fabrication. At knowledge level, the learner studies why temperature changes can alter dimensions, properties and the behaviour of fabricated components.

sections.heading: 2. Expansion and contraction
sections.body: Metals can change dimension as temperature changes. Heating is associated with expansion and cooling with contraction. In fabrication, these effects matter because uncontrolled dimensional change can affect fit, alignment and the final condition of an assembly.

sections.heading: 3. Thermal hazards require controls
sections.body: The curriculum identifies hazards associated with fire, equipment, ventilation, storage and consumables. The learning principle is that thermal work must be governed by approved workplace controls and competent supervision rather than improvisation.

sections.heading: 4. Heat treatment as a controlled process
sections.body: Heat treatment is used to influence material properties through controlled thermal cycles. Different methods serve different purposes. The Companion explains the principle only and does not provide practical treatment procedures, temperatures, timings or cooling instructions.

sections.heading: 5. Pre-heating and post-weld treatment concepts
sections.body: The curriculum requires understanding of the purposes and applications of thermal treatment before or after joining. At knowledge level, learners should recognise that such decisions depend on material, engineering requirements and approved procedures.

sections.heading: 6. Material structure and transformation
sections.body: Changes in temperature can affect the internal structure and properties of metals. Concepts such as phase transformation, cooling behaviour and transformation diagrams help explain why controlled thermal treatment matters. Their practical application requires formal technical instruction and approved data.

sections.heading: 7. Incorrect thermal control has consequences
sections.body: Uncontrolled heating or cooling can adversely affect a component or its properties. Learners should therefore understand that thermal decisions must be based on verified technical requirements rather than assumptions.

sections.heading: 8. Stop and refer uncertainty
sections.body: Where material information, approved procedures, equipment status or authority is unclear, the safe principle is to stop and refer the matter to a competent trainer or supervisor rather than attempt practical thermal work.
